page.layout: One page of text, one column. Running head at top: "De Episcopatu" left, "Q.XII." right, with page number 112 at the left edge. No marginal notes, no catchword, no signature.

main_text.p: facit Magistratui subjectus, ab eo dependens, tutus illo Euangelii vindice ac custode gladio, &c. & illustrat similI exemplo Aristotelis, Magistri Alexandri, cùm inquit: Potuit eodem tempore & regnum quoddam in artibus apud suum alumnum obtinere eique de totâ scientiarum ratione praecipere, & interim vel ipsius juvenis vel Philippi Patris altiori gubernationi subjici: sic etiam qui ipsos Magistratus docent res sacras, iisdem subjiciuntur & ab eorum auctoritate in exercitio pendent. Cl. Walæus ex professo totâ parte secundâ libri sui p. 51. &c. tractat hanc rem, & ostendit, quousque (sunt verba illius) officium ministrorum subjectum sit officio Magistratus; Et p. 64. dicit se quando ait ministrum non esse subditum aut servum Magistratus, loqui de partibus essentialibus, & substantia ministerii ipsorum, non autem de circumstantiis administrationis aut ministerii. Et p.67. ait: Reformatos Theologos non contradicere, si quis dicat ministros certo modo subordinatos dinatos

page.notes: Printed "subjectus" and the other long s forms are copied as plain s. The page number "51" after "p." is read from a small figure and may be "5l"; the reading 51 is my best reading. The word "Walæus" is set with a ligature and is read as Walæus. The last line is "subor-" with "dinatos" right-aligned; the hyphen is kept. The line "dinatos" appears on its own line at the right, so it is the end of the visible text on this page. The page is typeset in roman and italic, with no black letter and no Greek or Hebrew.
